I've been thinking about "why a buffer tube".

If you make a telescoping bolt like an Uzi, or use dual recoil springs like a Tec-9, you could potentially eliminate the buffer tube.

The buffer tube is the most retarded aspect of the whole design. I mean, it's a practical solution to the problem it addresses (keeping the receiver itself small and modular; keeping the mass of the moving parts low), but it's way past its time.

That spring has to go somewhere. The AK does it mostly right, but the long-stroke piston system and the added mass to the BCG slows down the rate of fire significantly. (600ish AK RPM vs 800-900 AR RPM, on full-auto, of course).

Plenty of companies make bufferless ARs. Rock River and Brownells immediately come to mind. There's a few others. Sig's MCX does it better than anyone, but it's really just an AK with two important differences:

  1. It's a short-stroke instead of a long-stroke piston system; and
  2. They use two springs instead of one to avoid infringing on Kalashnikov's patents. (If you've ever seen the spring setup for a P90 or PS90, it's almost exactly that.)

There are even cheats. Evolution Weapon Systems has caught my eye. Those conversions are expensive, but you are getting quite a bit for your money. The only problem is that they can't keep up with production. Maybe they'll get there one day.
